photon.title: Does a positive gap reduce modeled group speed?

notes.question: Can momentum loss at fixed propagation time discriminate zero-gap and positive-gap conditional histories?
notes.hypothesis: A positive rest-energy gap reduces final modeled group speed at fixed drag and duration.
notes.alternative: Zero-gap energy loss need not change group speed. An observed spectral shift alone cannot distinguish mechanisms.
notes.negative_control: Increase drag in the zero-gap control: speed remains C.
notes.positive_control: A larger gap at the reference drag should reduce group speed more.
notes.measurement_plan: Compare final group speed / C; a physical test would need independently calibrated path length, time of flight, energy and detector response.

escape.title: Does escape increase the final escaped population?

notes.question: Does the Markov escape term permit net escape in this selected-mode model?
notes.hypothesis: At the chosen interaction duration, nonzero escape gives a greater escaped population than the closed reference.
notes.alternative: Coherent closed conversion can oscillate without any escaped population. This endpoint does not test continuous individual photon slowing.
notes.negative_control: Change duration at zero escape: no escaped population.
notes.positive_control: Nonzero escape at ratio 8 should also yield large escaped population at GT=12.
notes.measurement_plan: Measure channel-resolved populations and loss independently; numerical endpoint alone cannot prove the physical reservoir or monotonicity.

timing.title: Does fixed transit delay preserve pulse spacing?

notes.question: Can a change of emitted spacing be distinguished from a constant transit delay?
notes.hypothesis: Increasing the emission interval increases the received interval by the same amount in the specified stationary-delay model.
notes.alternative: A constant delay shifts arrivals without stretching intervals. Moving endpoints or a time-varying channel require separate modeling.
notes.negative_control: Change only the constant transit delay: arrival spacing must be unchanged.
notes.positive_control: Use a larger emission interval to verify a known response.
notes.measurement_plan: Measure consecutive pulse arrival intervals using a calibrated clock and fixed endpoints; test channel stability independently.

distance.title: Does ignored attenuation bias inferred size?

notes.question: How does a signed unmodeled magnitude offset affect inferred/calibrated size?
notes.hypothesis: Positive attenuation ignored by the model increases the inferred/calibrated ratio.
notes.alternative: No offset leaves that ratio at one; real astronomical calibration can involve additional variables.
notes.negative_control: Vary calibrated distance with zero attenuation: the ratio remains one.
notes.positive_control: A larger positive offset should increase the ratio.
notes.measurement_plan: Use the ratio, not absolute distance, as primary endpoint. A physical study needs independent geometric anchors, calibrated flux, extinction and angular size.

geometry.title: Does a common translation preserve physical separation?

notes.question: Which changes affect Euclidean separation in the teaching model?
notes.hypothesis: Increasing horizontal separation at fixed vertical separation increases the invariant separation.
notes.alternative: A common coordinate translation changes coordinate labels without changing the separation; this does not establish a new theory of geometry.
notes.negative_control: Change the common origin offset only.
notes.positive_control: Increase horizontal separation further at fixed vertical separation.
notes.measurement_plan: Compare separation computed from calibrated coordinate differences. This is a geometric identity control, not a cosmological observation.
